sections.h2: Where in Delta County are deeds recorded?
sections.html:
Every deed in the county is recorded in Escanaba. The Register of Deeds works from the county building at 310 Ludington Street, open from eight to four, and the county line is (906) 789-5100, with a fax at (906) 789-5179.

That holds whether the house stands in Escanaba, in Gladstone, in the village of Garden, or out in a township near Rapid River or Rock. Call ahead about anything unusual. Bring the original signed deed and the fee, and ask whether the counter takes cards.

The office follows the statewide schedule in MCL 600.2567, which applies unless a charter county sets its own. Under it a deed is $30 to record whatever the page count.

Recording fees for an Escanaba closing
ServiceFee
Recording one document$30.00
Each additional instrument in an assignment or discharge$3.00
Photocopies$1.00 a page
Certifying a recorded paper$5.00
Records search on request$0.50 for each year, minimum $5
Filing another paper$1.00

Payment is due when you hand the paper to the clerk. An electronic filing that is also paid electronically can settle within one business day under the statute. Ask the office whether it accepts e-recording and through which vendors.

sections.h2: What transfer tax comes out of a Delta County seller's proceeds?
sections.html:
Sellers pay two charges. The state takes $3.75 and the county $0.55 for every $500 slice of the price, and a partial slice counts as a whole one. The county charge comes from MCL 207.504, MCL 207.523 makes the seller liable, and the county treasurer collects. Payment is due within 15 days of the buyer receiving the deed.

  • Exempt from the state tax: transfers under $100, security instruments, land contracts that hold back title until paid, and conveyances to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild.
  • Refunds: when tax was paid on a sale that later proves to qualify for an exemption, the seller, or a buyer who paid for the seller, may ask the Department of Treasury for the money back.
  • Value: the deed has to state it, or an affidavit declaring the value goes along with the deed.

The county list in MCL 207.505 is shorter. A family transfer can therefore avoid the state share yet still owe the county share, so check with the register before you sign.

sections.h2: Which deeds need a treasurer's certificate?
sections.html:
Most sale deeds do. Under MCL 211.135 the register must hold a deed, plat or land contract until the treasurer certifies tax liens and tax titles and confirms that five years of taxes are paid.

A quitclaim or other conveyance with no warranty covenants is excused, and so are sheriff's deeds and some state tax deeds. The county treasurer keeps county money, collects delinquent property taxes, certifies deeds and runs the annual tax sale for the State Treasury.

Before you pick a closing date, ask the treasurer what the certificate costs and how fast it is issued.

The Delta County Equalization office serves title agents and appraisers. Its price list shows a $5 Equalization Report, a $15 Apportionment Report listing millage rates, and $15 for taxable value broken out by school district or township. Database copies run $1 a page and simple maps $2.

A single house is different. For its assessed and taxable value, contact the assessor in the city or township where it sits. A buyer estimating the first tax bill will want those two numbers and the millage rate.

sections.h2: Recording a Delta County sale, start to finish
sections.html:
Think of the process as five steps. First, a title company or attorney prepares the deed, and each seller signs with a printed name under the signature. Second, a notary, judge or court clerk acknowledges the signatures. Third, the treasurer certifies taxes if the deed warrants title. Fourth, the closing agent works out the transfer tax from the full price and sets aside the recording fee. Fifth, the package goes to 310 Ludington Street in Escanaba, where the register records the deed.

Bring the original signed deed rather than a copy, along with the fee and any certificate. If the buyer is paying cash and no lender is involved, the deed and its fees are the whole recording package, which keeps the visit short.

Unpaid property tax is what most often holds up a deed. No certificate issues while a lien or balance is outstanding, and a warranty deed sits at the register until one arrives. Get a written payoff figure before choosing a closing date, and have the closing agent pay the balance from your sale proceeds. The certificate then comes back clean and nobody makes a second trip.

A cash buyer will usually want these loose ends tied up before the day of closing, so raise the tax question with your closing agent as soon as you accept an offer.

sections.h2: Delta County housing at a glance
sections.html:
The typical owner-occupied house is valued at $157,100, median rent is $692, and median household income is $57,809. Owners live in 82.0% of occupied homes. The county has about 36,582 residents spread over 1,171 square miles of land, so parcels range from city lots in Escanaba and Gladstone to farms and forest acreage.

For a seller the practical upshot is variety. A lakeside cottage near Escanaba, a house in Gladstone and forty acres near Garden call for different disclosures, surveys and legal descriptions, but all three travel to the same counter on Ludington Street for recording.

sections.h2: What formatting does a Delta County deed need?
sections.html:
One recording format applies across Michigan under MCL 565.201, and the Escanaba office enforces these items.

  • Ink signatures, each with a printed name beneath it, and names that match from the body of the deed to the notary block.
  • A street address for every party, and the drafter's name with a way to reach them.
  • For a deed signed in Michigan, an acknowledgment taken by a notary, judge or court clerk.
  • 2.5 inches left blank at the top of page one for the recorder's stamp.
  • No more than four trailing digits of a Social Security number.

Counter staff neither write deeds nor give legal advice. If you inherited the house, ask the title company whether a death certificate or court order has to be recorded before the deed. Sorting that out early keeps an estate sale from stalling at the counter.

faqs.q: How much does the Delta County register charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars a document, per MCL 600.2567. A release naming several instruments adds $3 for each extra, and certifying a recorded paper costs $5.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on a Delta County house sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. The state rate is $3.75 and the county rate 55 cents for every $500 slice, payable to the county treasurer inside 15 days of delivery.

faqs.q: Do deeds for Gladstone and Garden homes go to Escanaba?
faqs.a: Yes. The register at 310 Ludington Street records for the entire county, including both cities and the village.

faqs.q: Is a quitclaim deed exempt from the treasurer's certificate in Delta County?
faqs.a: Yes, when it has no warranty covenants. A warranty deed or land contract must carry the certificate before the register will accept it.

faqs.q: What are the register's hours in Escanaba?
faqs.a: Eight to four. Telephone (906) 789-5100 to confirm holiday closures.
